l1: What Windows Server version and build is the DNS server running? (Get-ComputerInfo | Select OsName,OsVersion,OsBuildNumber)
Is the DNS Server role installed on a standalone server or co-hosted on a Domain Controller? (Get-WindowsFeature DNS)
Is the zone configuration file-backed (Standard Primary) or Active Directory-Integrated? (Get-DnsServerZone | Select ZoneName,ZoneType,IsDsIntegrated)
How many DNS servers are deployed in the environment — are they AD-integrated replicas, secondary servers, or standalone?
What is the exact symptom — resolution timeout, SERVFAIL, NXDOMAIN, wrong IP returned, or zone not loading?
What is the Event ID reported by the DNS Server service in Event Viewer? (Applications and Services Logs > DNS Server)
When did the issue first occur — after Windows Update, zone configuration change, AD replication failure, or network infrastructure change?
Is the problem affecting all DNS queries globally, specific record types (A, AAAA, MX, PTR, SRV), specific zones, or specific clients?
Is the DNS Server service currently running and set to Automatic startup? (Get-Service DNS | Select Name,Status,StartType)
Are there error events in DNS Server event log? (Get-WinEvent -LogName 'DNS Server' -MaxEvents 50)
Is this DNS server also a Global Catalog server? Could GC unavailability affect LDAP lookups for AD-integrated zones?
Is the DNS server reachable on UDP/TCP port 53 from affected clients? (Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <DNS IP> -Port 53)
Are there multiple network interfaces on the server — could DNS be listening on the wrong interface?
l2: What zone types are hosted — Forward Lookup, Reverse Lookup, Stub Zones, Conditional Forwarders, or Secondary Zones?
For AD-integrated zones: what is the replication scope — DomainDNSZones (domain-wide), ForestDNSZones (forest-wide), or Custom Application Partition?
Are there zone delegation NS records pointing to child zones — are the delegated name servers responsive and authoritative?
What forwarders are configured — global forwarders or conditional forwarders per domain? Are they reachable on UDP/TCP 53?
Is recursion enabled on this server? (Get-DnsServerRecursion | Select RecursionAvailable, RecursionTimeout) — if disabled, clients cannot use it for recursive resolution.
Are DNSSEC zones configured — what signing algorithm (RSASHA256, ECDSAP256SHA384), NSEC/NSEC3, and key rollover status? (Get-DnsServerDnsSecZone)
Are DNS Policies configured for application load balancing, subnet-based filtering, or split-brain DNS? (Get-DnsServerQueryResolutionPolicy)
Is Response Rate Limiting (RRL) enabled — could it be throttling clients behind NAT sharing a source IP? (Get-DnsServerResponseRateLimiting)
What are the DNS aging and scavenging settings — No-Refresh interval, Refresh interval, Scavenging period? Is scavenging enabled server-wide or per-zone?
Is the DNS server listening on all IP addresses or specific interfaces? (Get-DnsServerSetting | Select ListenAddresses) — recent NIC changes may affect binding.
Is DNS debug logging enabled — what log level flags (0x8100F331) and maximum file size? (Get-DnsServerDiagnostics)
Is split-horizon DNS configured — internal and external views of the same zone with different records?
Are DNS socket pool, cache locking, and EDNS0 enabled for cache poisoning protection? (Get-DnsServerSetting | Select SocketPoolSize,CacheLockingPercent)
What is the TTL configuration for dynamically registered records — is it consistent with DHCP lease durations and scavenging intervals?
Are Windows Firewall rules blocking DNS port 53 inbound/outbound? (Get-NetFirewallRule | Where DisplayName -like '*DNS*')
Is the DNS server configured with root hints or forwarders only? (Get-DnsServerRootHint vs Get-DnsServerForwarder)
Are there DNS query statistics showing high failure rates? (Get-DnsServerStatistics)
Is the DNS server experiencing high CPU or memory utilization? (Get-Counter '\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time', '\Memory\Available MBytes')

l1: Run 'nslookup <failing hostname> <DNS server IP>' — share full output including server, address, and any error (Non-existent domain, Timeout, Server failed, Refused).
Run 'Resolve-DnsName <hostname> -Server <DNS IP> -Type A' — share PowerShell output with IP address and response time.
Run 'Get-Service DNS | Select Name,Status,StartType,ServiceType' — confirm DNS Server service is running and set to Automatic.
Run 'ipconfig /all' on the DNS server — confirm server's own IP configuration, subnet mask, default gateway, and its DNS server settings.
Is the issue reproducible from multiple clients or only one — helps confirm if the server is the problem vs. client-side cache or network issue?
Run 'Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <DNS IP> -Port 53' from an affected client — confirm TCP 53 is reachable (DNS uses TCP for responses >512 bytes and zone transfers).
Run 'nslookup -type=SOA <zone name> <DNS IP>' — verify SOA record is returned correctly (confirms zone is loaded and authoritative).
Has restarting the DNS Server service temporarily restored resolution? 'Restart-Service DNS' — if yes, may indicate a transient state or memory leak.

Export DNS Server event log entries from the time window when the issue started — look for Event IDs 4000 (zone load failed), 4001 (zone write failed), 4004 (zone cannot load), 4013 (DNS server waiting for AD).
l2: Run 'dcdiag /test:dns /v /f:C:\dcdiag_dns.txt' — share the full text file; note all FAIL and WARN entries, especially delegation and record registration issues.
Run 'repadmin /showrepl * /csv > C:\repadmin_showrepl.csv' — check for AD replication failures across all DCs (AD-integrated zones require healthy replication).
Run 'dnscmd /enumzones' — share the zone list with ZoneType, ZoneDP, and ReplicationScope for each zone.
Run 'Get-DnsServerZone | Select ZoneName,ZoneType,ReplicationScope,IsDsIntegrated,IsAutoCreated,IsReverseLookupZone,IsDynamicUpdateEnabled | Format-Table -AutoSize' — share full output.
Run 'Get-DnsServerDiagnostics | Format-List *' — share all diagnostic/logging flags including LogLevel and EventLogLevel.

Enable DNS debug logging: 'Set-DnsServerDiagnostics -All -LogLevel 0x8100F331 -EventLogLevel 0x8100F331' — reproduce for 5-10 minutes — disable: 'Set-DnsServerDiagnostics -LogLevel 0x0' — share C:\Windows\System32\dns\dns.log.
Run 'Get-DnsServerForwarder' — list all forwarders; test each: 'Test-NetConnection <forwarder IP> -Port 53' — ensure they are reachable.
Run 'Get-DnsServerRecursion | Select RecursionAvailable,RecursionTimeout,AdditionalRecursionTimeout' — confirm recursion settings match intended design.
Run 'Get-DnsServerRootHint' — verify root hints are present and contain the 13 root name server IP addresses (a.root-servers.net through m.root-servers.net).
Run 'Get-DnsServerStatistics -ZoneName <zone>' — review TotalQueries, TotalResponses, TcpQueries, UdpQueries, RecursionFailures, SecureUpdateFailures for anomaly patterns.
Run 'Get-DnsServerZoneTransfer -ZoneName <zone>' — confirm zone transfer settings (SecureNotify, TransferToAnyServer, NotifyServers) for secondary zones.
Run 'Get-DnsServerResourceRecord -ZoneName <zone> -RRType NS' — verify NS records are current and pointing to authoritative name servers.
Run 'Get-DnsServerCache | Select -First 50' — inspect cached records for stale entries or negative cache entries (NXDOMAIN) that may be causing false failures.
Run 'Get-DnsServerDnsSecZone -ZoneName <zone>' — review DNSSEC signing state, Key Signing Key (KSK), Zone Signing Key (ZSK), and rollover status.
Run 'Get-DnsServerQueryResolutionPolicy' and 'Get-DnsServerQueryResolutionPolicy -ZoneName <zone>' — list all server and zone-level DNS policies for split-brain or filtering.
Run 'Get-DnsServerSetting | Select ListenAddresses,EnableIPv6,AllowUpdate,DisableAutoReverseZones' — verify server-level configuration.
Run 'Get-Counter '\DNS Server\Total Queries Received', '\DNS Server\Total Responses Sent', '\DNS Server\Recursive Queries/Sec' -SampleInterval 5 -MaxSamples 10' — assess query load patterns.

l1: Verify DNS Server service is started and set to Automatic: 'Set-Service DNS -StartupType Automatic; Start-Service DNS' — confirm Event ID 4 (DNS Server started) appears in DNS Server event log.
Check zone loading: 'Get-DnsServerZone | Where ZoneType -eq "Primary"' — verify all expected zones are loaded with IsDsIntegrated and IsAutoCreated states.
Test resolution locally on the DNS server itself: 'nslookup <hostname> 127.0.0.1' — if works locally but not from clients, the issue is network connectivity or firewall, not DNS server.
Test forwarder reachability: 'Test-NetConnection <forwarder IP> -Port 53' — if unreachable, external name resolution will fail; update forwarders or fix network path.

Review Event ID 4013 (DNS server waiting for Active Directory) — occurs when AD replication is incomplete at DNS service startup. Resolution: ensure AD is healthy, then 'Stop-Service DNS; Start-Service DNS'.
Flush the DNS server cache: 'Clear-DnsServerCache -Force' — clears all cached records including stale or negative entries; retry the failing query immediately after.
Verify server is domain-joined with valid credentials: 'nltest /sc_verify:<domain>' and 'klist' — expired Kerberos tickets or broken secure channel prevent AD-integrated zone loading.

Check Windows Firewall rules: 'Get-NetFirewallRule | Where DisplayName -like "*DNS*"' — confirm inbound rules for UDP/TCP 53 are enabled and set to Allow on the appropriate profile (Domain/Private/Public).
l2: If AD-integrated zone fails to load (Event 4000/4001): verify DNS partition exists in AD — 'repadmin /showattr . DC=DomainDNSZones,<domain> /atts:objectClass' — if missing, restore from system state backup or recreate zone.

If zone records are being scavenged prematurely: check per-record timestamp vs. No-Refresh interval — 'Get-DnsServerResourceRecord -ZoneName <z> -RRType A | Select HostName,Timestamp' — increase No-Refresh interval or disable scavenging on critical records via 'Set-DnsServerZoneScavenging'.

If recursion fails for external names: test root hints — 'Resolve-DnsName . -Type NS -Server <DNS IP>' — timeout indicates broken root hints or blocked UDP 53 outbound. Rebuild root hints: 'Import-DnsServerRootHint -NameServers (Resolve-DnsName . -Type NS | Where Type -eq A).NameRecord'.

If DNSSEC validation fails (SERVFAIL on DNSSEC-signed zone): verify trust anchor — 'Resolve-DnsName <zone> -DnssecOk -Server <DNS IP>' and compare with 'Get-DnsServerDnsSecZone' trust anchor state; ensure DNSKEY records are present and not expired.

If DNS Policy is misdirecting queries: 'Get-DnsServerQueryResolutionPolicy' — verify SubnetList matches the failing client's source IP subnet; check for conflicting policies where order matters (first matching policy wins).

If split-brain DNS divergence causes wrong records for internal clients: compare SOA serial numbers — 'Resolve-DnsName <zone> -Type SOA -Server <internalDNS>' vs '<externalDNS>' — if external serial > internal, zone transfer from external is stale; force zone transfer: 'Invoke-DnsServerZoneTransfer -Name <zone> -FullTransfer'.

If DNS debug log shows REFUSED (RCODE 5): server is refusing queries from that source IP — check DNS server's Recursion scope (Get-DnsServerRecursion) or Query ACLs (Get-DnsServerQueryResolutionPolicy); ensure client subnet is allowed.

If Response Rate Limiting (RRL) is dropping legitimate queries: 'Get-DnsServerResponseRateLimiting' — review WindowSize, LeakRate, TruncateRate, and WhitelistTable; add internal subnets to whitelist: 'Add-DnsServerResponseRateLimitingExceptionList -Subnet <CIDR>'.

If AD replication is causing inconsistent DNS records across DCs: force replication — 'repadmin /syncall /AdeP' — then verify record consistency across all DNS servers with 'Get-DnsServerResourceRecord'.

Use pktmon to capture DNS traffic for packet-level analysis: 'pktmon filter add -p 53; pktmon start --capture; <reproduce>; pktmon stop; pktmon etl2txt pktmon.etl' — analyze for RCODE values in response packets (0=NOERROR, 2=SERVFAIL, 3=NXDOMAIN, 5=REFUSED).

If DNS server is experiencing high CPU/Memory: analyze performance counters — 'Get-Counter '\DNS Server\Total Queries Received', '\DNS Server\Recursive Queries/Sec', '\Process(dns)\% Processor Time' -SampleInterval 5 -MaxSamples 20' — consider offloading queries to additional DNS servers or enabling DNSSEC only on authoritative zones.

If EDNS0 (Extension Mechanisms for DNS) is causing issues with legacy devices: disable EDNS0 temporarily — 'Set-DnsServerSetting -EDns0Outbound $false' — but be aware this limits packet size to 512 bytes and may cause truncation for large responses.

l1: Export DNS Server event log: 'wevtutil epl DNS-Server-Service C:\DNS_Server_Events.evtx' — contains critical events for zone loading, AD integration, and query failures.
Run 'ipconfig /all > C:\dns_server_ipconfig.txt' — capture server IP configuration including DNS server settings, which should point to itself or another internal DNS server.
Run 'Get-DnsServerSetting | Out-File C:\dns_server_settings.txt' — export server-level configuration including listen addresses, recursion, and EDNS0 settings.
Run 'nslookup <failing name> <DNS IP> > C:\nslookup_test.txt' — document the exact failure mode for troubleshooting reference.
Run 'Get-DnsServerZone | Export-Csv C:\dns_zones.csv -NoTypeInformation' — export all zone configurations including type, replication scope, and dynamic update settings.
l2: Enable DNS debug logging: 'Set-DnsServerDiagnostics -All -LogLevel 0x8100F331 -EventLogLevel 0x8100F331' — reproduce for 5-10 minutes — disable: 'Set-DnsServerDiagnostics -LogLevel 0x0' — collect C:\Windows\System32\dns\dns.log for detailed query analysis.
Run 'dcdiag /test:dns /v /f:C:\dcdiag_dns.txt' — comprehensive DNS diagnostics including delegation tests, record registration verification, and AD integration checks.
Run 'repadmin /showrepl * /csv > C:\repadmin_showrepl.csv' — AD replication status across all DCs; critical for AD-integrated zone health.
Capture network trace: 'netsh trace start capture=yes tracefile=C:\dns_trace.etl maxsize=1024 overwrite=yes' — reproduce the issue — 'netsh trace stop' — analyze with Message Analyzer or Wireshark.
Run 'Get-DnsServerStatistics | ConvertTo-Json | Out-File C:\dns_statistics.json' — export DNS server performance metrics for load analysis.
Export all zone data: 'ForEach ($z in (Get-DnsServerZone).ZoneName) { Export-DnsServerZone -Name $z -FileName "C:\$z.dns" }' — creates zone export files in standard DNS format.
Run 'Get-DnsServerDiagnostics | Out-File C:\dns_diagnostics.txt' — export current diagnostic logging configuration.
Collect System and Application event logs: 'wevtutil epl System C:\System_Events.evtx'; 'wevtutil epl Application C:\App_Events.evtx' — for service startup and system-level errors.
Export DNS cache: 'Get-DnsServerCache | Export-Csv C:\dns_cache.csv -NoTypeInformation' — capture cached entries to identify stale or negative cache poisoning.
TSS full data collection: '.\TSS.ps1 -Scenario NET_DNSsrv' — run on the DNS server, reproduce the issue, stop when prompted — collects comprehensive logs for Microsoft Support analysis.

steps.expect: Status: Running, StartType: Automatic — service must be operational
TcpTestSucceeded: True — confirms TCP 53 reachable (DNS uses TCP for large responses and zone transfers)
Returns valid A record — if timeout, SERVFAIL, or NXDOMAIN, server-side issue confirmed

steps.action: nslookup <failing name> 127.0.0.1 on the DNS server itself
steps.expect: If resolves locally but not from clients, network or firewall is blocking port 53 to clients

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName 'DNS Server' | Where Id -in 4000,4001,4013 | Select -First 10 | Format-List
steps.expect: Event 4013 = waiting for AD; 4000/4001 = zone load failure; determines root cause
All expected zones present and loaded — missing zones indicate AD integration or zone file issues
Cache cleared immediately — retry resolution to eliminate stale cache as cause
Service restarts cleanly — verify Event ID 4 (DNS Server started) in DNS Server event log
Inbound rules for port 53 TCP and UDP are Enabled and Allow on appropriate profile
Returns correct IP address with reasonable response time

steps.action: Test from two clients on different subnets
steps.expect: Both resolve correctly — confirms server-wide fix, not network-specific
Zone should appear in output — if missing, it failed to load from AD partition

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName 'DNS Server' | Where Id -in 4000,4001,4013 | Select -First 10 | Format-List
steps.expect: Event 4013 = waiting for AD (service waiting for AD replication); 4000/4001 = zone load failure
No replication failures across all DCs — if failures exist, fix AD replication first as DNS zones depend on it
Secure channel to DC is healthy — broken secure channel prevents AD zone access
Valid Kerberos tickets present — if expired, run 'klist purge' then 'gpupdate /force' to refresh
DNS service restarts after AD is confirmed healthy — zone loads on startup from AD partition
Forces full zone transfer from primary — for AD zones, this reloads from AD partition
Zone present with IsDsIntegrated: True and correct replication scope
Record resolves correctly with correct IP address

forwarder_unreachable.title: External name resolution failing — forwarder unreachable

steps.expect: If timeout or SERVFAIL for external names but internal names work, forwarder issue confirmed
Lists configured forwarder IPs — verify they are the intended servers
TcpTestSucceeded: True — if False, forwarder is unreachable due to network or firewall
RecursionAvailable: True — if False, recursion is disabled, preventing external resolution even with working forwarders
Replace unreachable forwarder with a reachable one — test with public DNS (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1) as fallback
Root hints present for fallback recursion if forwarders are removed or fail — DNS falls back to root hints when forwarders unavailable
External name resolves successfully with correct IP address
Multiple external domains resolve — confirms fix is not specific to one domain

dnssec_validation_failure.title: DNSSEC validation failing — SERVFAIL on signed zones

steps.expect: If SERVFAIL with DNSSEC validation, DNSSEC issue confirmed
Check DNSSEC signing state, KSK/ZSK status, and trust anchor configuration
DNSKEY records present and not expired — if missing or expired, validation fails
Trust anchor configured for the zone — missing trust anchor causes validation failure
Rotate signing keys if expired — ensure new keys are propagated to trust anchors
Configure correct trust anchor if missing or incorrect
Returns AD (Authenticated Data) flag indicating successful DNSSEC validation
Records resolve successfully without SERVFAIL
